feed.title: Smart Glasses & Wearables — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Meta Ray-Ban Display
entry.content:
Meta’s display glasses controlled by an EMG wristband. Compared with touch or voice control, it shows where the input method is heading; the ecosystem is closed.

https://www.meta.com/tr/ai-glasses/meta-ray-ban-display-shiny-sand-transitions-and-neural-band-sand/

entry.title: Brilliant Labs
entry.content:
A glasses maker that publishes both hardware schematics and software. Unlike closed makers such as Meta, it is close to the only company in the sector selling a product while opening the design.

https://brilliant.xyz/

entry.title: Açık Kaynak Gözlük Yaptık
entry.content:
A video on building open-source glasses. Unlike success-story showcases it is honest about which parts are genuinely hard — worth watching before committing to the project.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4ZY760EIUc4

entry.title: Akıllı Gözlük Yapımı
entry.content:
A step-by-step build starting from components rather than a kit. The optical combiner and power management sections are the hard parts.

https://www.instructables.com/Smart-Glasses-V2/

entry.title: GitHub · ray-ban-meta
entry.content:
Community projects around Ray-Ban Meta glasses. Unlike Meta’s official access toolkit, the work here is mostly protocol analysis and unofficial bridges — still active because the official toolkit is new and limited.

https://github.com/topics/ray-ban-meta

entry.title: Açık Kaynak Gözlük Yapımı
entry.content:
A step-by-step build guide for open-source smart glasses with a bill of materials and assembly order. Unlike project showcases it has that level of detail — exactly what makes the project reproducible.

https://github.com/Mentra-Community/OpenSourceSmartGlasses/wiki/How-to-build-the-Open-Source-Smart-Glasses/4f426a4923cd6265b6179954e8abb2e6308b893a

entry.title: Mentra Bluetooth SDK
entry.content:
A starter kit for connecting to glasses over BLE from Android. Unlike writing BLE code from scratch, the GATT services and characteristics arrive defined, so you do not reverse-engineer the protocol.

https://github.com/Mentra-Community/Mentra-Bluetooth-SDK-Starter-Kit

entry.title: MentraOS
entry.content:
An open operating system for smart glasses unifying different vendors’ hardware under one app layer — aimed at the problem of writing a separate app per device.

https://github.com/Mentra-Community/MentraOS

entry.title: Omi
entry.content:
A wearable that listens to conversations and summarises them, capturing context rather than vision. The ethics of always-on listening are a separate argument.

https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi

entry.title: OpenGlass
entry.content:
Converts an existing pair of glasses by attaching a camera and board, on a parts list of roughly $25. Conversion rather than manufacture.

https://github.com/BasedHardware/OpenGlass

entry.title: Open Source Smart Glasses
entry.content:
An all-day wearable open-source glasses design with schematics, PCB and software published — so unlike closed products you can see what it collects and where it sends it.

https://github.com/Mentra-Community/OpenSourceSmartGlasses

entry.title: GitHub · smart-glasses
entry.content:
A live list of tagged open-source projects that stays current by itself, unlike curated lists — the way to catch new arrivals.

https://github.com/topics/smart-glasses

entry.title: HeyCyan Wi-Fi Aktarım Mimarisi
entry.content:
A technical note on how media transfer from glasses to phone is structured — control over BLE, bulk data over Wi-Fi. A pattern directly applicable to similar devices.

https://github.com/ebowwa/HeyCyanSmartGlassesSDK/blob/main/WIFI_TRANSFER_ARCHITECTURE.md

entry.title: HeyCyan Web Köprüsü
entry.content:
Connects HeyCyan glasses to a browser over Web Bluetooth. Instead of writing a native app you talk to the device from the browser — a fast route for prototyping.

https://github.com/AdeelHamid/HeyCyan-Web-Bridge-App

entry.title: Alternatif HeyCyan Uygulaması
entry.content:
An open-source alternative to the vendor app, aimed at unlocking restricted features and removing the cloud dependency.

https://github.com/FerSaiyan/Alternative-HeyCyan-App-and-SDK

entry.title: HeyCyan SDK
entry.content:
A cross-platform SDK for HeyCyan glasses. Unlike the vendor’s closed app, it lets your own application control photo, video and audio capture.

https://github.com/ebowwa/HeyCyanSmartGlassesSDK

entry.title: Brilliant Labs Halo
entry.content:
AI glasses where a developer can load their own applications — unlike closed ecosystems, the right to run code on the device is yours.

https://brilliant.xyz/products/halo

entry.title: Akıllı Gözlük İşletim Sistemleri
entry.content:
A comparison of Horizon OS, Android XR and the other smart-glasses platforms; which ecosystem to invest in comes before hardware selection. Unlike a single platform’s pitch it sets them side by side — though bear in mind it is a glasses maker’s blog.

https://dymesty.com/blogs/articles/smart-glasses-operating-system-guide

entry.title: Giyilebilir Yonga Setleri
entry.content:
An article on the graphics-versus-power trade-off in high-end wearables; in display glasses the GPU choice sets battery life directly. Unlike product reviews it looks from the chip-design side — bear in mind the author is a GPU vendor.

https://blog.imaginationtech.com/chipsets-for-smart-glasses-and-other-high-end-wearables/

entry.title: PSOC4 CAPSENSE Uygulama Notu
entry.content:
An application note on adding touch control to a glasses temple, with circuit diagram and calibration parameters. Unlike general datasheets it is concrete — documentation at this level is rarely public.

https://www.infineon.com/assets/row/public/documents/30/42/infineon-an242193-smart-glasses-hmi-with-psoc4-capsense-applicationnotes-en.pdf

entry.title: RealMCU Akıllı Gözlük
entry.content:
A vendor offering low-power glasses silicon aimed at simpler, cheaper devices than Qualcomm. For glasses that only show notifications, a Snapdragon is overkill.

https://www.realmcu.com/en/Applications/Smart-Glasses

entry.title: Qualcomm AI Glasses
entry.content:
The official page for the Snapdragon AR platform inside most shipping glasses, with reference designs and power figures. Unlike individual product pages it looks at the platform level — for understanding what is inside which glasses.

https://www.qualcomm.com/xr-vr-ar/applications/ai-glasses

entry.title: Akıllı Gözlük Yonga Rehberi
entry.content:
A comparison of processors and NPUs used in glasses, weighing power budget and thermal limits — in a frame the real constraint is heat, not compute.

https://dymesty.com/blogs/articles/smart-glasses-processor-chip-guide

entry.title: Even G2 Protokolü
entry.content:
Reverse-engineering of the device’s BLE protocol — the only route to uses the official SDK does not permit.

https://github.com/i-soxi/even-g2-protocol

entry.title: Awesome Even Realities G2
entry.content:
A community resource collection for the Even Realities G2 smart glasses. Unlike the official documentation, this is where the tools and solved problems it does not cover accumulate.

https://github.com/pangoleen/awesome-even-realities-g2

entry.title: Even Realities (GitHub)
entry.content:
Even Realities’ official repositories and the primary source for the SDK and sample apps. Unlike glasses makers that keep code closed it publishes — still the exception in this sector.

https://github.com/even-realities

entry.title: Even Hub
entry.content:
Even Realities’ developer hub, holding app development resources and API documentation. Unlike its GitHub repositories, it gathers documentation and guidelines rather than code.

https://hub.evenrealities.com/?_gl=1*rku60w*_gcl_au*MTY2MjM2NDk0LjE3ODUwODM2MjY

entry.title: Even Realities · Çerçeve Seçimi
entry.content:
Frame and prescription lens options — the part that decides whether the glasses actually get worn daily, more than the technology does.

https://www.evenrealities.com/smart-glasses/selection

entry.title: Even Realities G2
entry.content:
Everyday glasses with a display and deliberately no camera. The omission is a decision rather than a shortfall — it addresses the social acceptance problem head on.

https://www.evenrealities.com/smart-glasses
